newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cattle ship picks up boatpeople off Australia.
newsitem.headline: Cattle ship picks up boatpeople off Australia.

text.p: A ship carrying cattle from Australia to Indonesia was forced to return to port on Thursday after picking up 70 boatpeople believed to be from China, a government spokesman said.

Australia's immigration department said the boatpeople -- 38 men, 15 women and 17 children -- could be from a boat which was stranded with engine trouble off the Indonesian resort island of Lombok last month.
"It's a pretty good guess and that boat has been in Indonesian waters the last couple of weeks," an immigration department spokesman told Reuters. "The numbers seem to add up."
"We'll talk to them tonight, make sure they get a good medical examination and then start asking them where they're from," he added.
The group that had been stranded off Lombok told Indonesian authorities they were from China and bound for New Zealand.
Australia's customs surveillance agency on Tuesday picked up a distress signal from an unidentified boat in Australian waters 180 nautical miles northwest of Darwin in northern Australia.
Maritime rescue officials then contacted the Liberian-registered Anomis, which picked up the group early on Wednesday morning.
The Australian navy inspected the craft carrying the boatpeople and ordered it scuttled after deciding it was a navigation hazard.
The Anomis had been heading for Indonesia but returned to Australia after its captain determined there was not enough food on board for his crew and the extra 70 people.
In recent years hundreds of boatpeople have travelled through the Indonesian archipelago on their way to Australia or New Zealand.
The immigration department spokesman said 264 Chinese boatpeople had landed in Australia on four different boats in May and June last year.
